source: Liu, Qu, Schneider, Singh, Kumar (2025) CaRT: Teaching LLM Agents to Know When They Know Enough
finding: CaRT fine-tunes a small model on counterfactual trajectory pairs (one where stopping is right, a minimally edited one where it is not) plus a written reason for the decision. It beats base and plain SFT on stop timing in medical diagnosis and math.
numbers: Qwen2.5-3B-Instruct for diagnosis; 2,000 DeepScaleR problems with Qwen3-1.7B traces for math; eval on AIME 2025. CIs over 30 eval runs and 3 training seeds. Train mix 80% continue / 20% terminate.
limits: Only a small model; results mostly in figures, few headline numbers; RL post-training made conversations longer.
agent_relevance: Template for S8: train or probe a stop decision using paired stop vs continue prefixes, with a stated reason.

source: CaRT (2025) label definition for terminate
finding: A prefix is labeled terminate only if stopping now gives clearly higher success than continuing. For diagnosis, optimal stop = one Q/A pair raises free-response success by at least 50%. Hard negatives are built so success falls below 30%.
numbers: Oracle label uses an external diagnostic model: about 20% free-response success with full info, under 40% with preliminary info.
limits: Oracle labels depend on an external model that may itself be wrong.
agent_relevance: Stop labels need an outcome-based oracle, not model self-report. Fits G3: check on something the answer was not fitted to.

source: CaRT (2025) ablation: counterfactuals and reasoning
finding: Removing counterfactual data hurts most. Removing reasoning traces also hurts. Reasoning smooths the stop-probability curve across a conversation, reducing abrupt flips.
numbers: Table 1, 102 held-out conversations: direct accuracy 0.567 (base), 0.849 (CaRT minus reasoning), 0.663 (CaRT). Logistic-probe test accuracy 0.581, 0.645, 0.774 (70/30 split). Row labels in the extracted table were ambiguous; order inferred from the text.
limits: Probe test set is tiny; direct accuracy is higher without reasoning, so the reasoning benefit shows only in the probe.
agent_relevance: A written reason may regularize the stop decision, but do not assume it raises raw accuracy.

source: CaRT (2025) out-of-distribution and RL results
finding: On out-of-distribution dermatology diagnosis, base and SFT models did worse than even a naive fixed-question-count stop rule; CaRT still beat it, with a smaller gain. RL post-training pushed toward longer episodes and gave no math gain.
numbers: AIME 2025: CaRT gets higher accuracy with fewer tokens than base and SFT (figure only).
limits: Absolute gain shrinks under domain shift.
agent_relevance: A learned stop rule can be worse than a fixed budget off-distribution; keep a fixed budget as a floor.

source: Chen et al. (2024) Do NOT Think That Much for 2+3=? On the Overthinking of o1-Like LLMs
finding: First study of overthinking in o1-like models: easy problems get lots of extra compute with little benefit. Self-training that shortens traces keeps accuracy on GSM8K, MATH500, GPQA, AIME.
numbers: Abstract only read this session; no numbers recorded.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Motivates a difficulty-aware stop: easy items should exit early.

source: Yang et al. (2025) Dynamic Early Exit in Reasoning Models (DEER)
finding: Training-free. At reasoning transition points the model drafts a trial answer; if its confidence is high, generation stops. Works across 11 reasoning models and 10 benchmarks.
numbers: CoT length cut by 19.1% to 80.1% on average; accuracy change +0.3% to +5.0%. DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen series: MATH-500 average accuracy 83.55 vanilla to 84.45 DEER; AIME 2024 43.35 to 51.05. DEER-Pro: length cut 19.1%-42.9%, only 2.8%-6.2% longer than DEER, higher accuracy, fixes prompt sensitivity in small models.
limits: Depends on a trial-answer prompt; small models are prompt-sensitive; AIME 2025 averaged over 4 sampling rounds.
agent_relevance: Direct fit for S8: probe a trial answer, stop if confidence is high. Needs a check beyond self-confidence (G2, G4).

source: Mitigating Overthinking in LRLMs via Reasoning Path Deviation Monitoring (RPDI-EE, 2026)
finding: Argues that answer-confidence early exit over-truncates: models show spurious confidence and are silenced before self-correction. Proposes exit when high-entropy transition tokens (Wait, But) pile up, i.e. the model is truly stuck.
numbers: Eight reasoning models; benchmarks GSM8K, AMC23, MATH500, AIME24/25, OlympiadBench, GPQA-Diamond. Compared mainly with vanilla CoT and DEER. Claims largest accuracy gain over vanilla CoT but smaller token savings than aggressive methods.
limits: Authors' own claim; compared only against DEER among strong baselines because of compute limits.
agent_relevance: Warns that trial-answer agreement is not proof of sufficiency; pair stop signals with an external check.

source: Entropy After </Think> (EAT) for reasoning model early exiting (2025)
finding: Append the stop-thinking token and watch the entropy of the next token. Entropy falls and stabilizes when pass@1 plateaus; thresholding its variance under an exponential moving average gives a stop rule. Works with a proxy model for black-box reasoners.
numbers: MATH500 and AIME2025: 12-22% fewer tokens with no accuracy harm; up to 21% in the proxy setup. Models include DeepSeek-R1-0528-Qwen3-8B and R1-Distill-Llama-70B.
limits: Savings are modest; needs logits (or a white-box proxy).
agent_relevance: Cheap stop signal that needs no sampling rollouts; the program, not the model, reads it.

source: Akgul et al. (2025) LYNX: Learning Dynamic Exits for Confidence-Controlled Reasoning
finding: A probe on hidden states at cue tokens ('wait', 'hmm') predicts whether forced exit would be right. Split conformal prediction gives a distribution-free bound on premature exits. One math-trained probe transfers across tasks.
numbers: Models: R1-1.5B, QwQ-32B, Llama-3.1-Nemotron-8B. GSM8K: 40-65% fewer tokens, accuracy matched or better. MATH-500: up to +12 points with 35-60% fewer tokens. AIME 2024: baseline accuracy with over 50% saving. CommonsenseQA zero-shot: modest gain, up to 70% fewer tokens.
limits: Needs open weights; the guarantee covers premature-exit rate, not task accuracy.
agent_relevance: A calibrated stop rule with a user-set error rate; the conformal idea suits a budget guardrail.

source: Thought calibration: Efficient and confident test-time scaling (2025)
finding: Lightweight probes on hidden states decide when thinking can stop, calibrated so performance is preserved. Three probes: supervised correctness, answer consistency, and lack of new reasoning-tree leaves.
numbers: Three reasoning models, four datasets: up to 60% fewer thinking tokens in-distribution (held-out s1K), up to 20% out-of-distribution.
limits: The supervised probe was over-confident because the test set has unsolvable problems.
agent_relevance: Stop rules must handle unsolvable items; otherwise correctness probes keep spending.

source: Reasoning Models Know When They're Right: Probing Hidden States for Self-Verification (2025)
finding: A probe on hidden states predicts correctness of intermediate answers with high accuracy and calibrated scores, and even before the answer is written. Used as a verifier to exit reasoning.
numbers: 24% fewer inference tokens with no performance loss.
limits: Needs hidden states and labeled training data.
agent_relevance: Models encode sufficiency internally but do not act on it; supports reading it out by program.

source: Answer Convergence as a Signal for Early Stopping in Reasoning (2025)
finding: On math, models usually reach their final answer after about 60% of the reasoning steps. Three fixes: stop on answer consistency, boost end-of-reasoning probability, learn a stop probe.
numbers: Five benchmarks, five open-weight LLMs. NaturalQuestions: Answer Consistency cuts tokens by over 40% and improves accuracy.
limits: Math-centered finding; consistency can lock in a wrong answer.
agent_relevance: Supports a rule: stop when the same answer repeats across checkpoints, with an outside check.

source: Li et al. (2024) Escape Sky-high Cost: Early-stopping Self-Consistency (ESC)
finding: Sample in small windows and stop when a window is unanimous. Cuts sample count at similar accuracy.
numbers: Sample reduction: MATH -33.8%, GSM8K -80.1%, StrategyQA -76.8%, CommonsenseQA -78.5%, Coin Flip -84.2%, Last Letters -67.4%. Abstract only read.
limits: Abstract only; same-model samples are correlated so unanimity is weak proof (G4).
agent_relevance: Cheap vote-level stop rule for sampling states.

source: Aggarwal, Madaan, Yang, Mausam (2023) Let's Sample Step by Step: Adaptive-Consistency
finding: Stop sampling when a statistical test on the answer distribution says the leader is stable. Budget cut by up to 7.9 times with under 0.1% average accuracy drop.
numbers: 17 reasoning and coding datasets, three LLMs. Abstract only read.
limits: Abstract only; assumes independent samples, which same-model samples are not.
agent_relevance: A Bayesian-style sequential stop rule the program can compute.

source: Li et al. (2024) MediQ: Question-Asking LLMs and a Benchmark for Reliable Interactive Clinical Reasoning
finding: Plain prompting to ask questions makes models worse than answering from initial info. An abstention module (1-5 confidence rating, rationale, self-consistency of 3) decides when to keep asking and improves accuracy.
numbers: Best expert: +22.3% over the BASIC interactive setup and +12.1% over the non-interactive Initial setup; still a 10.3% gap to the full-information upper bound. Most models rarely ask follow-up questions. Models over 70B beat the Initial setup with best abstention; smaller ones do not. Self-consistency alone hurt unless paired with rationale.
limits: Simulated patient system; small models stayed behind.
agent_relevance: Prompted stop-asking decisions are weak; a confidence scale plus rationale is the best prompted fix.

source: Hu et al. (2024) Uncertainty of Thoughts (UoT): Uncertainty-Aware Planning Enhances Information Seeking
finding: Simulates future question paths and rewards expected information gain to choose the next question; improves success and needs fewer questions in diagnosis, troubleshooting and 20 Questions.
numbers: Average +38.1% task completion rate over direct prompting across multiple LLMs. Abstract only read.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Information-gain framing is the classical OR stop rule: stop when expected gain falls below cost.

source: Muennighoff et al. (2025) s1: Simple test-time scaling (budget forcing)
finding: Budget forcing cuts thinking off by force or extends it by appending 'Wait'. s1-32B scales AIME24 from 50% to 57% with extra thinking and exceeds o1-preview by up to 27% on MATH and AIME24.
numbers: 1,000-example s1K fine-tune of Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct. Abstract only read.
limits: Abstract only; stopping is forced, not learned.
agent_relevance: The fixed-budget baseline that learned termination must beat; the RPDI paper says such methods can degrade accuracy in some settings.

source: Does Thinking More always Help? Mirage of Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning Models (2025)
finding: Extra thinking raises accuracy first and then lowers it. A simple model says extra thinking adds output variance, which looks like gains and then hurts precision. Parallel thinking works better for the same budget.
numbers: Abstract only read.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Supports an upper cap on thinking even for hard items.

source: Inverse Scaling in Test-Time Compute (2025)
finding: On crafted tasks, longer reasoning lowers accuracy. Five failure modes: Claude gets distracted, o-series overfits framing, spurious correlations, loss of focus on deduction, and amplified concerning behaviors.
numbers: Four task categories. Abstract only read.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Longer is not safer; justifies a stop signal tied to evidence, not to elapsed effort.

source: Graves (2016) Adaptive Computation Time for Recurrent Neural Networks
finding: Older system: the network learns how many compute steps to take per input via a halting unit. Big gains on synthetic parity, logic, addition, sorting; little gain on character-level language modeling.
numbers: Abstract only read.
limits: Abstract only; halting is inside the network, not a text-level decision.
agent_relevance: Ancestor of learned termination; helps most on algorithmic tasks.

source: Banino, Balaguer, Blundell (2021) PonderNet: Learning to Ponder
finding: Learns the number of steps with a probabilistic halting rule trained end to end. Beats ACT on a synthetic task, matches state of the art on a QA dataset with less compute, and extrapolates.
numbers: Abstract only read.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Halting as a learned probability fits a program-held stop gate.

source: Stop Overthinking: A Survey on Efficient Reasoning for LLMs (2025)
finding: Survey that sorts efficient-reasoning work into model-based, output-based (dynamic step reduction at inference) and prompt-based methods. Early exit sits in the output-based group.
numbers: Abstract only read.
limits: Abstract only.
agent_relevance: Map of the field to check for missed methods.

source: Wald (1945) sequential tests; Chow-Robbins optimal stopping; secretary problem (background)
finding: Classical stopping theory: stop when the likelihood ratio crosses a threshold set by error costs (SPRT), or when expected gain from one more sample drops below its cost. The secretary problem gives a 1/e rule for single choice.
numbers: From background knowledge; not opened this session.
limits: Not opened; needs known likelihoods, which LLM samples do not supply.
agent_relevance: The OR baseline that learned termination approximates; gives a principled threshold form for S8.

source: Session note: gap in direct tests of human-versus-LLM stopping paradigms
finding: In my searches I found no study that gives LLMs the classic human optimal-stopping tasks (secretary, sampling-cost tasks) with a measured human comparison. The 2024-2026 work is engineering of early exit and question-asking. The arXiv search API returned empty and Semantic Scholar rate-limited, so this absence is not proven.
numbers: None.
limits: Search coverage limited by tool failures.
agent_relevance: Treat human-vs-LLM stopping comparisons as unknown, not as absent.

source: BLADE: Boundary-Expanded and Layer-Adaptive Dynamic Exit for Efficient LLM Reasoning (2026)
finding: Frames early exit as predicting whether the current prefix is already sufficient; picks probe layers adaptively and needs consecutive confirmations before stopping.
numbers: Reported 24.8% token reduction on Qwen3-8B with accuracy largely preserved (search snippet only).
limits: Seen only in a search result summary; not opened; arXiv ID looks unusual, verify before citing.
agent_relevance: Consecutive-confirmation stop is a simple hysteresis rule a program can apply.
